origin_result.basis: Final manufacture took place in the UAE; manufacturing goes beyond the minimal operations; all 2 non-originating inputs are classified outside subheading 320910; value addition build-down is 65.0% against a threshold of 40% on an FOB basis. Totals: price basis FOB; 4 inputs, of which 2 non-originating; non-originating inputs are 35% of the price.

procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory (the exporter must apply; registration takes about 3 working days and requires the factory to be outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added).
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The exporter ensures the final manufacture of the goods takes place in the UAE.

The exporter ships the goods directly from the UAE to India; if transit through another country is necessary, the goods must remain under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. If a third party issues the invoice, the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.
The exporter logs in to the ministry e-services portal and chooses the Certificate of Origin for India service.
The issuing authority requires the application to include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product; each item must qualify separately in its own right.
The exporter uploads proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 (band: invoice value up to AED 100000; the service fee range is AED 10 to AED 200).

The competent authority issues the certificate before, at, or within five working days of the date of exportation; it is valid for twelve months from issue and covers only one import. If the certificate is issued after export, it may be marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 (Remarks) of India's certificate form, up to twelve months from the date of shipment.
The exporter prints the approved certificate.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing; the importer must answer a customs request within ten working days.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years starting from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

caveats.note: Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Indian inputs count as originating only with proof of their originating status (bilateral cumulation, Art. 3.7).
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
By interpretation, de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
Minor typing or formatting errors on the certificate are tolerated; discrepancies in signature or seal are not.
An issued certificate can be amended once, for a fee of AED 20; the invoice amount and the destination cannot be changed.
